title: Shilluk kingdom founded
description: By tradition the culture hero Nyikang leads his people north to the White Nile and founds a divine kingship that endures into the nineteenth century.

title: Ali Khurshid pushes south
description: As the Funj kingdom falls to Egypt, Ali Khurshid Pasha leads troops up the White Nile into the Dinka lands, opening the south to conquest and the slave trade.

title: Region opened to merchants
description: Under foreign pressure Cairo opens the Upper Nile country to European merchants and missionaries, and traders' ivory and slave posts follow.

title: Gordon governor of Equatoria
description: Charles George Gordon takes charge of the new Equatoria province and wages war on the slave traders from his post on the Nile.

title: Aliab Dinka attack
description: Three thousand Aliab Dinka overrun a police post near Bor while the Mundari attack telegraph linesmen, the high point of armed resistance to British rule.

title: Southern Policy
description: The British bar northern traders and officials from the south and administer it as a separate world, freezing the gulf between north and south.

title: Southern Policy reversed
description: Without asking southerners, the administration switches to uniting the south with the north, setting up the tensions of independence.

title: Anyanya opens the war
description: The Anyanya separatists launch their first organised attacks on the Sudanese army, turning scattered resistance into an insurgency.

title: Autonomous region abolished
description: President Nimeiry dissolves the Southern Sudan Autonomous Region and imposes sharia on the whole country, stripping the south of the self-rule won in 1972.

title: Nasir split
description: Riek Machar leads a faction out of John Garang's SPLA, turning much of the liberation war into a south-against-south fight armed by Khartoum.

title: Bor massacre
description: Machar's forces kill several thousand Dinka civilians around Garang's home town, a wound that poisons southern politics for decades.

title: Machakos Protocol
description: The government and the SPLA agree for the first time that the south will vote on its own independence, the breakthrough that leads to the 2005 peace.

title: Independence referendum
description: Nearly 99 percent of southern voters choose secession, and their country becomes the world's newest state in July.

title: UN membership
description: Five days after the proclamation of independence, South Sudan is admitted as the 193rd member state of the United Nations.

title: Heglig crisis
description: South Sudanese and Sudanese forces battle over the oil field of Heglig in the sharpest fighting between the two states since independence.

title: Civil war begins
description: Fighting between guards loyal to Kiir and to Machar in Juba slides the country into a civil war that eventually kills some 400,000 people.

title: Bentiu massacre
description: Rebels hunting down victims by ethnicity in mosques, churches and hospitals kill hundreds after taking the oil town of Bentiu.

title: Compromise Peace Agreement
description: Under intense international pressure, Kiir and Machar sign a power-sharing deal that briefly brings Machar back to Juba as vice-president.

title: Revitalised peace deal
description: A revitalised agreement shares power again between Kiir, Machar and other factions and largely quiets the war.
